findings.original_behavior: The actual Host wrapper treated an empty command list as settled, marked accounting complete and released the quality-check reservation despite explicitly unknown started execution.
findings.impact: Worker/project/platform capacity could be reclaimed while checker execution/result remained unverified. This is a resource-ownership correctness defect in the trusted wrapper, not an Agent-created PROCESS privilege.
findings.recommendation: Release only explicit known-not-started reports or completed non-INCONCLUSIVE invocations with nonempty command evidence and observed close; otherwise retain UNKNOWN.
findings.fix_author: Parent/root implementation author; reviewer made no implementation change
findings.fixed_behavior: Explicit execution_started=false + zero commands + BLOCKED may settle. Started execution requires nonempty commands, a non-INCONCLUSIVE result and every close_observed; all other combinations retain UNKNOWN_QUARANTINED.
findings.reproduction: Import the actual openHarness module; create an isolated synthetic project and BACKGROUND_REVIEWER with bounded budgets; call administration.runPilotQualityCheck with an in-memory report callback; inspect actual resource_reservation rows. No checker/child process/model/Provider is invoked.
findings.preservation: Pre-fix and post-fix tool observations are embedded here with exact source hashes. The original and recheck temporary SQLite/Artifact directories were closed and deleted after each validation; this report does not claim those temporary DBs still exist.

latest_code_review.detail: Latest index.ts only adds explicit budget_state to the quality-check record/event at this boundary. The noInvocation/completedInvocation predicates and UNKNOWN/settle actions remain identical to the exact 0d8e6db48ddb9441601a6ba9365a55415aaa5a3c1fbeb0d8dde1826a1299a2bc source exercised by the retained three-case actual negative recheck. This latest source hash is code-review coverage; it is not substituted into historical runtime output.

checks.detail: Budget reserve and durable intent precede the synchronous fixture callback. Callback throw/Promise/schema/usage failures preserve SENT, sequence, key occupancy and UNKNOWN quota. Recover does not dispatch or release old claims; only explicit KNOWN_NOT_SENT/AUTH simulation can advance the route. Existing models TAP contains all 34 passing cases, including negative/fault/cancellation paths.

The responder receives frozen subject/request/public model definition and independently reconstructed context; detached callback invocation supplies no privileged receiver. Model/key/admin/Store/credential handles are not added to its input. Registration accepts only provider-bound vault:mock opaque handles; there is no HTTP/SDK/real-provider adapter. Agent facade inspection in the recheck exposes no administration/models/gates/checker object.

Model input is independently reconstructed and hash-bound before reserving or dispatching. Development admission requires a persisted successful model result owned by the exact subject, a Task-history source and the exact original requirement source in the proposer context. Plan outputs, case/prefix collisions, DAG, read-only roles and aggregate requests/disk are bounded by the Host envelope; a model strategy never becomes an execution permission.

Subagent tool/resource/file/read scopes are constrained to the existing parent grants. Read-only roles cannot receive write tools, and NativeToolRuntime always rejects PROCESS/EXTERNAL_EFFECT or unverified sandbox execution. A model proposal is data; local writes still traverse exact Gateway approval, Feature/Policy, intent and storage/Gate bindings.

Scheduler recovery deletes approval_id on pending tools and returns approval-required work to an explicit Host lane. Message wakes resume only WAIT with no pending tool/reservation; APPROVAL_REQUIRED, HANDOFF, PAUSED, UNKNOWN and recovered DISPATCHING intents are not automatically replayed. Existing event TAP includes approval wait, cancelled/UNKNOWN and real close/reopen/process-kill cases.

Only an acknowledged durable message reaches the Host onDeliverable hook; it creates a deduplicated internal event binding message ID and payload hash. Existing dispatch receives/leases the current inbox and atomically adopts message payload into Task history with receipt/ACK. A settled wake is explicitly separate from Task completion and Gate acceptance; external-effect retry is prohibited and idle wake control performs no model call.

Gate evaluation and checker/human-review registration require the trusted admin capability. Native PASS binds Task/rule registry, candidate, baseline, test profile and control epochs. G3 requires a registered TEST checker; G4 requires an independently bound reviewer. SIMULATED checker/model-shaped PASS artifacts cannot directly create a protected Native Gate PASS. Exact write candidate hashes are checked again at Task execution.

The independently confirmed P1 was fixed by the implementation author. Started+INCONCLUSIVE reports retain UNKNOWN even when they declare a closed command. Explicit BLOCKED/not-started reports can release known unused capacity. The final current index.ts was fully re-read after the parent added budget-state observability; unchanged decision predicates remain covered by the preserved exact-hash recheck.

assumptions_and_limits: This is independent engineering review of the listed other-author source paths, not evidence that an AgentNexus Pilot Agent autonomously performed the review.

Programmable responder and registered checker callbacks are trusted Host code. JavaScript callback purity, privileged closure capture and the Host-supplied responder source hash are not enforced or proven by an OS sandbox.
Authorized context content may itself contain Host-provided data; the reviewed responder constructor does not inject credential/key handles, and no real credential or Provider was accessed.

The fixed checker implementation and its authored tests are explicitly excluded from this independent coverage. The Host wrapper was tested using synthetic report metadata, with no checker invocation.

Budget mode and accounting source remain SIMULATED local ledger semantics. No cumulative CPU, hostile-process isolation, descendant-tree exit, network boundary, reboot, power loss or production deployment qualification is inferred.
The scheduler was read only in the explicitly listed relevant line ranges; this is not a fresh full-tree independent review or full-regression rerun.
Actual model and event TAP files were inspected as existing evidence. Their earlier failures and inherited platform limits are not overwritten or upgraded by this report.
The exact pre-fix temporary DB was deleted, so the preserved historical negative evidence is the tool-observed output and original source hash embedded in this report.
